statement.pnt_input: There exist d0,C,x0>0 such that |A(x)| <= C x exp(-d0 f(log x)) for x>=x0, with f(v)=v^(3/5)(log v)^(-1/5). This follows from Bellotti's unconditional optimal Korobov-Vinogradov-scale PNT error, after absorbing floor(x)-x.
statement.moving_cutoff: There exists C0>0 such that U_n=C0 n^5 [log(n+e)]^2 and X_n=exp(U_n) satisfy d0 f(v) >= 4 sqrt(n v) for every n>=1 and all v>=U_n.
statement.ordered_tail: T_n(X_n) := lim_{Y->infinity} sum_{X_n<m<=Y} a_m b_n(m) exists in natural m-order.
statement.tail_bound: For a constant C1 independent of n, |T_n(X_n)| <= C1 (n + n^(3/2) sqrt(U_n)) exp(-2 sqrt(n U_n)). Hence T_n(X_n) is smaller than every negative power of n, and in particular is <= C2 exp(-kappa n^3 log(n+e)) for suitable C2,kappa>0.
statement.scope: This is only a source-order tail certificate. It does not bound the moving finite prefix, prove any Li coefficient positive, or imply RH.

derivation.formula: For finite Y>X, sum_{X<m<=Y} a_m b_n(m) = A(Y)b_n(Y)-A(X)b_n(X)-integral_X^Y A(t)b_n'(t) dt.

derivation.authority: elementary coefficient formula plus I_0(2sqrt(nu)) <= exp(2sqrt(nu))

derivation.formula: d/du L_{n-1}^{(1)}(u)=-L_{n-2}^{(2)}(u) for n>=2, and |L_{n-2}^{(2)}(u)| <= n^2 exp(2 sqrt(nu)); therefore |b_n'(t)| <= 2 n^2 t^(-2) exp(2 sqrt(n log t)), with n=1 checked directly.
derivation.authority: standard Laguerre derivative identity plus elementary coefficient bound

derivation.formula: f(v)/sqrt(v)=v^(1/10)(log v)^(-1/5) is increasing for v>e^2. At U_n=C0 n^5 log^2(n+e), its value is a positive C0^(1/10)-multiple of sqrt(n) up to a bounded logarithmic ratio. Choose C0 so d0 f(U_n)>=4 sqrt(n U_n); monotonicity then gives d0 f(v)>=4 sqrt(nv) for all v>=U_n.

The boundary obeys |A(X_n)b_n(X_n)| <= C n exp(-2 sqrt(nU_n)). With v=log t, the derivative integral is <=2C n^2 integral_{U_n}^infinity exp(-2 sqrt(nv))dv =2C n^2( sqrt(U_n)/sqrt(n)+1/(2n))exp(-2sqrt(nU_n)).

negative_comparator.input: For a logarithmic zero-free region nu(t)=c/log t, the Ingham optimization omega(x)=min_y {c log(x)/y+y}=2sqrt(c log x). Bellotti-Trudgian-Yang 2026 provides the explicit c=1/4.896 region.
negative_comparator.comparison: The same crude Laguerre boundary envelope has exponent -2sqrt(c v)+2sqrt(nv)=2(sqrt(n)-sqrt(c))sqrt(v), so this operator/majorant family does not force boundary decay once n>c.
negative_comparator.scope_limit: This falsifies only logarithmic-zero-free-region + this crude Laguerre-envelope routing. It is not a no-go theorem for the 2026 zero-free result or for sharper transforms.
